blocks.text:
Anyone their neighbors dislike, anyone with a middling bit of money: they're all on edge, wondering when someone will inform on them. (The truly rich, mind you, hand the Church a fortune in advance, so it seems they never come to trial.)

Everyone dreads being informed on by everyone else, and in their fear they pin false charges on others... It's becoming an age when you can't trust even your parents, your brothers or your lover. The only one who profits is the Church.

Oh yes, in the far north, a lord who'd come to distrust everyone around him reportedly went so far as to slaughter 40 percent of his subjects. That's a good deal more dangerous than any monster.

That reminds me: monsters hardly figure at all in the news that drifts in here lately. Their numbers ought to be growing, not shrinking, but human savagery catches the eye far more. No, I'd say the people it has actually harmed are far more numerous, too.

Has the terror of monsters woken the "instincts of a carnivore" that slept in humankind for a thousand years?... What a foul world this truly is.

Sorry to write of nothing but dark things. I hope that next time I can write of something brighter.
Olterna E. Tassel, Tassel Trading House

To the residents of the Coffin of Kars

The miracle of angels descending is happening all over the world. I've seen it with my own eyes, and it moved me, I'll tell you. The sky suddenly shines, angels appear, and they wipe out the monsters in an instant. Dreadful as those monsters are, they're no match at all for the angels.

The one thing that grates a little is the Church going around advertising it as its own doing, but thanks to the angels, most of the town of Lanz is back in the hands of almighty humankind.

At last the enemy is no longer "monsters" but "humans" themselves. Asroit is turning from four powers into three. The one that dropped out is Wettin. Of the three remaining dukes, Duke Durer, with the infamous Red Lion Knights at his back, has taken the east and southeast of Asroit in hand, which I'd say puts him a step ahead.

Baileste, the greatest city in the world, is reportedly a shadow of itself after the rebel army's looting. The Republic of Baileste's army has vanished completely too; its units have as good as sunk to mountain banditry.

From Asroit, from Baileste, from every other country, talk of war flies in day after day. The weapons I buy from you are probably being used less against monsters than in wars between humans. To find you've become a "merchant of death" before you knew it is a rather nasty feeling.

The angels' arrival is happy news, but it has made the Holy Tribunal suddenly much fiercer as well.

The terror of monsters, the Holy Tribunal, and now war... You can't trust anyone, not even your family or your lover. This age is far too cruel for people to live in. Which is exactly why more and more people, high and low alike, are leaning on the Anoian faith to hold them up. Their piety must be beyond comparison with what it was in the peaceful days.

And into all that come the angels. Like it or not, faith can only climb higher.

No one speaks of the Church's decadence and corruption anymore. Not a soul. Everyone is desperate to find favor with God. There's no way the Church won't make use of that. The Holy See and the bishoprics everywhere have begun executing heretical sects and anti-Pope factions one after another, in the name of the Holy Tribunal.

Even in the cities of the former Baileste and of Fisano, which never had anything to do with the Holy Tribunal, I hear it's now in full swing.
So this time, I suppose, it's half bright news and half dark. Whatever else may be, it's good to sleep in my own house. I greet the night with thanks for the power of the angels.
Olterna E. Tassel, Tassel Trading House

To the residents of the Coffin of Kars

The Pope's power has become the eye of the storm.

Wielding military and political strength with skill, he is bringing the cities of the former Republic of Baileste under his rule one after another. In only a month, nearly half of the Republic's home territory has fallen into the Pope's hands.

Thanks to the weapons called "Magic Tools" and "Spell Devices," the way war is waged is changing too. You needn't be any good with a sword or spear: with these two, even a child makes a fine fighter.

In fact peasant soldiers, until now mere numbers to fill the ranks, are outperforming the nobles' regular armies. (Those regular armies being a pack of dregs to begin with, it's only natural they've been overtaken.)

Knights were dropped from the lead role on the stage of war long ago. Peasant soldiers armed with Magic Tools and Spell Devices: they're war's leading players now. Anyone can join a war with no real training, so the numbers in a single battle easily run into the thousands, even tens of thousands. With wars this much bigger, naturally the dead keep piling up too. The fight between Pfalz and Wettin drew a staggering 220,000 men on the two sides combined, with 70,000 dead, they say. The coffin makers must be raking it in.

The number of Magic Tools will likely decide the battles to come.

So which side holds the most of them... You'd think the nobles of old Baileste and old Asroit, but to my surprise, they say it's the Pope's army. It seems the Pope's army had been hiding Magic Tools in such quantity that you have to wonder when it gathered them. That must be the secret of the Pope's great leap forward.

I meant to move on to news from each region, but frankly, there's too much to write.

After all, between my last letter and today, the news of battles with over 10,000 men in them easily tops 50. Some reports must never have reached this town, so who knows how many times that the real figure is... Mere skirmishes no longer even come up in the talk of traveling merchants. The world truly is all war and nothing else. The Holy Tribunal's fever hasn't cooled either, and the descent of the angels, our one comfort, seems rather fishy according to your letters... What on earth will become of this world...
Olterna E. Tassel, Tassel Trading House
To the warriors of Kars

The angels saved people from the terror of monsters, took a firm grip on everyone's hearts, and then one day vanished without a trace. But the plain fact that the angels are gone has cast a dark shadow over people's minds.

The war only grows fiercer and there's no way out in sight. The monsters may be somewhat fewer, but they haven't been wiped out, and the Holy Tribunal shows no sign of ending. In this hopeless world, people's only salvation is the teachings of God.

But for many people, losing the angels, a miracle they could see with their own eyes, was as good as losing what held up their hearts and kept them living.

At such a time, let the Church declare that it happened because people's faith fell short, that God has run out of patience with humankind, and everyone is left with no choice but to believe in God with all their being.

You may laugh, but this is reality. When you face hunger and the terror of war every day, believing in God becomes a means of survival. Even the Bailesteans, rational as they're supposed to be, are like this.

As if stricken with a fever, the whole world is swearing obedience to the Church. If I didn't know what has gone on in your town, if I hadn't read the letters from Qumran-sensei and old Eugen, I doubt I could have stayed this calm.

Now for news from each region. That said, it's all about the Pope's army.

The Pope's army has invaded southwestern Asroit and southeastern Racoss. The Duke of Fakolz and Duke Ascania have both sworn obedience to the Pope. The petty nobles left in Racoss and western Asroit will all fall in line, I expect.

When the Pope's army first marched there was some real fighting, but now it isn't even a contest. No one is left who can check its momentum.

But though they've sworn obedience to the Pope, Fakolz and Ascania, at each other's throats as ever, haven't stopped their war.

The Pope's army has the military and political strength to stop it, yet shows no sign of doing so. Stranger still, Pope Gregorius VIII, that very incarnation of greed, is leaving the right to govern each region with its nobles. It almost looks as if he's parading around the world solely to advertise the greatness of God.

There's too much I don't understand. I'd seek advice, but everyone around me is a dog of the Church. What on earth will become of this world...
Olterna E. Tassel, Tassel Trading House

To the warriors of Kars

This will likely be my last report.

The assets of every trading house in this town are to be seized by the Church. There's a great deal I'd like to tell you, but I have no time to write it.

I pray for your success.
Olterna E. Tassel, Tassel Trading House
